statusSemantics.blocked-external: Needs a capability that does not exist in this repository or on this machine; Maestro keeps refusing.
statusSemantics.fixable-in-maestro: A named Maestro seam can close it; an owner task is assigned.
statusSemantics.partially-fixable: Maestro can tighten the refusal; full qualification still needs external evidence.
statusSemantics.refused-safely: The managed operation is refused before any effect; a safety pass, not functional parity.

requirements.requirement: Per-effect authorization of a running managed Grok turn by a real endpoint authority.
requirements.surface: desktop process manager, portable runAgentTurn, Cue
requirements.reason: The spawn authority's effects default to unavailableEffectAuthority: the endpoint exposes no per-effect authorization operation in this build. Managed Grok ACP permission requests are all denied; headless Grok asks no one.
requirements.requiredAuthority: Endpoint per-effect operation (CP-01, CP-03, owner mega-maestro) paired with this host and exercised against an exact Grok binary.
requirements.releaseImpact: Managed standard-mode Grok cannot complete a turn that needs any tool approval; no managed effect-enforcement claim.

requirements.requirement: Preventive control of provider-internal tool, file, shell, network and descendant effects on the managed child-process route.
requirements.reason: The child-process row is managed 'implemented' for launch admission only; headless Grok runs with --always-approve (batchModeArgs equals yoloModeArgs) or plan mode, and resolves its own permission prompts.
requirements.requiredAuthority: A confinement or per-effect producer for the route; until then Maestro must refuse managed operations whose policy requires preventive control (GT1-09-07).
requirements.releaseImpact: Launch admission is the only managed guarantee on headless Grok.

requirements.requirement: Qualified read-only semantics (files, symlinks, temporary files, shell descendants, network) for Grok.
requirements.reason: readOnlyCliEnforced is true on the strength of Grok's own --permission-mode plan plus --deny Bash(*); this is provider self-enforcement, not a Maestro sandbox, and is not proven on an exact binary per OS.
requirements.requiredAuthority: Exact-binary live qualification per OS (phase 11) or a host confinement producer.
requirements.releaseImpact: Read-only cannot be certified as a security boundary.

requirements.requirement: Proof that Grok ACP permission requests precede every effect class, with a typed effect a policy can decide.
requirements.reason: Each request becomes a 'permissions' effect carrying the raw request; title, kind and rawInput are deliberately not trusted as a classifier. Coverage of hooks, subagents, MCP meta-tools and provider network is unproven.
requirements.requiredAuthority: Live evidence that the exact binary asks before each effect class; a typed mapping only after that evidence exists.
requirements.releaseImpact: ACP availability is not a policy boundary for Grok.

requirements.requirement: The managed route table names the Grok ACP route and the ACP spawn is held to its own row.
requirements.surface: providerRouteSupport consumers (process manager, inventory, install policy, probes, cross-agent router)
requirements.reason: ManagedRoute has no ACP member; a managed ACP turn rides the child-process row and GrokAcpSpawner.spawn does not consult the table. The admitted snapshot names the headless argv while the spawner runs the ACP argv derived from it.
requirements.requiredAuthority: None for the table; a managed 'implemented' ACP row still needs GT1-09-R01.
requirements.releaseImpact: Fleet inventory and policy cannot see which Grok route ran.

progress.detail: ManagedRoute and MANAGED_ROUTES gain 'grok-acp' (capabilities.ts): standalone implemented for grok and unsupported for every other provider, managed unsupported with the R01/R06 gap as its note. src/main/process-manager/types.ts adds runsOnGrokAcpRoute(config) (the same rule as wantsGrokAcp) and managedGrokAcpRefusal(config) (an admitted ACP spawn returns { state: 'unavailable', code: 'capability-unsupported' } from the table, no fallback to headless). GrokAcpSpawner.spawn does not call it yet; continuation GT1-09-02B wires it. Fleet inventory now reports the grok-acp row for every provider through MANAGED_ROUTES.

requirements.requirement: Managed Grok ACP binds to a qualified version range, not to the version the peer reports.
requirements.surface: Grok route selector, desktop and portable
requirements.reason: The desktop snapshot starts with agentVersion null and completeGrokAcpNegotiation adopts the peer's reported version; only an absent version is refused.
requirements.requiredAuthority: A qualified version range from exact-binary live evidence; Maestro can refuse managed ACP until one exists.
requirements.releaseImpact: A new Grok release would run under management without new qualification.

progress.detail: The grok-acp managed row stays unsupported because the version is the peer-reported one, so a managed ACP turn is refused before negotiation instead of adopting it (after GT1-09-02B). The standalone selector still adopts the reported version; a qualified range needs GT1-11-12 live evidence.

requirements.requirement: The desktop dispatch snapshot carries the effective Grok model and account so a policy pin can see them.
requirements.reason: modelFromArgs reads --model and --model= only; Grok's modelArgs and model argBuilder emit -m <model>, so every Grok desktop snapshot has model null. The snapshot names no account.
requirements.requiredAuthority: None. The fix lives in src/main/process-manager/ProcessManager.ts, outside GT1-09-02's two named files, so it needs a bounded continuation task.
requirements.releaseImpact: An enterprise model pin cannot be enforced against a Grok desktop launch from the snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Managed Grok over SSH binds the actual remote target and its endpoint identity.
requirements.reason: Headless over SSH is admitted only with a bound sshRemoteEndpoint; ACP over SSH is refused (GROK_ACP_PORT_SUPPORT.remote false). No paired remote endpoint attestation producer exists here.
requirements.requiredAuthority: Remote endpoint attestation from an enrolled remote runtime; Maestro lineage and target binding in GT1-09-09.
requirements.releaseImpact: Managed remote Grok is refused unless a remote endpoint qualifies it.

requirements.requirement: Managed control of Grok MCP servers and MCP meta-tools.
requirements.reason: The Grok MCP entry is verified false with no qualified versions, so production Grok runs uninjected; native trust facts are reported, not enforced.
requirements.requiredAuthority: Exact-binary MCP loading, trust and disable evidence (phase 11); blocker grok-native-mcp-unqualified.
requirements.releaseImpact: No managed MCP claim for Grok.

requirements.requirement: Native Grok subagent effects governed under management.
requirements.reason: Subagent lineage is synthetic from pinned variants; subagent effects are provider-internal.
requirements.requiredAuthority: Native subagent evidence and per-effect authority; blocker grok-native-subagent-unqualified.
requirements.releaseImpact: No managed subagent claim for Grok.

requirements.reason: Grok has no verified all-off tool switch (no noToolsArgs); plan mode plus --deny Bash(*) is not no-tools. The groomer refuses requireDisabledTools since GT1-08-14.
requirements.requiredAuthority: A verified all-off flag on an exact binary.
requirements.releaseImpact: Safety pass; the functional no-tools guarantee stays absent.

requirements.requirement: Pre-effect DLP and control of the provider process's own network.
requirements.reason: Maestro's egress gate governs Maestro-owned fetches only; no DLP producer acts before a Grok effect.
requirements.requiredAuthority: A DLP and network control producer at a real sink.
requirements.releaseImpact: No DLP or provider-network guarantee for Grok.

requirements.requirement: A real endpoint admission decision for a Grok launch, with audit attribution.
requirements.reason: No enrolled endpoint exists on this machine and this phase enrolls nothing; admissions are exercised only against local or fake authorities.
requirements.requiredAuthority: Enrolled installation, live endpoint and registered actor (phase 11 GT1-11-12).
requirements.releaseImpact: Fake-authority tests prove client wiring only.
